card.title: Nuclear Density; Mass Number; Atomic Number

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Every nucleus is labelled by **atomic number Z** (protons — fixes the element and chemistry) and **mass number A** (protons + neutrons; A = Z + N), written $_{Z}^{A}X$ (uranium-238: Z = 92, N = 146). Scattering data show the radius grows as $R = 1.2A^{1/3}$ fm, so volume ∝ A while mass ∝ A — hence **nuclear density ≈ 2×10¹⁷ kg/m³ is the same for every nucleus**: nuclear matter is effectively incompressible.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Constant Nuclear Density: The result ρ ≈ constant applies to all nuclei (light and heavy) — strong evidence that nuclear force saturates and nucleons are tightly packed.  ·  Approximate Radius Formula: R = R₀A^(1/3) is empirical, valid for A > ~10. Very light nuclei show deviations.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The mass number A equals the number of protons plus neutrons; the atomic number Z equals the number of protons."

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Z defines the element; A defines the isotope** — chemistry follows Z, nuclear behaviour follows A.  ·  **Radius grows as A^(1/3), not A** — that cube root is why density stays constant.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Atom's ID Card Two integers — Z and A — identify any nucleus completely. Z fixes the element and its chemistry; A fixes the isotope and its nuclear behaviour. And the pair explains why all nuclear matter packs to the same astonishing density.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Atomic number and mass number - **Atomic number Z:** the number of protons — defines the element and its position in the periodic table; equals the nuclear charge +Ze and, for a neutral atom, the electron count. - **Mass number A:** the total number of nucleons (protons + neutrons); A = Z + N. - Notation: $_{Z}^{A}X$ — e.g. $_{92}^{238}U$ has Z = 92, A = 238, N = 146.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Show the density derivation in two lines: mass ∝ A, volume ∝ A.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Nuclear matter is incompressible** — mass ∝ volume at fixed density.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: A = Z + N; R = 1.2A^(1/3) fm; ρ ≈ 2×10¹⁷ kg/m³ for all nuclei.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A sugar-cube of nuclear matter would mass about a billion tonnes.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### Deep dive: Z, A and the density that never changes The atomic number Z counts protons and fixes the element's identity; the mass number A counts nucleons (protons + neutrons). Isotopes share Z but differ in A (¹H, ²H, ³H); isobars share A but differ in Z (¹⁴C and ¹⁴N). Nuclear mass is measured in atomic mass units, 1 u = 1.6605×10⁻²⁷ kg.…  ·  **Z, A, N — the nuclear bookkeeping** | Symbol | Meaning | Example (²³⁸U) | |---|---|---| | Z (atomic number) | proton count = element identity | 92 | | N (neutron number) | neutron count | 146 | | A (mass number) | Z + N nucleons | 238 | | Isotope | same Z, different A | ²³⁵U vs ²³⁸U | | Isobar | same A, different Z | ¹⁴C vs ¹⁴N |  ·  **Nuclear size and density formulas** | Quantity | Formula | Value | |---|---|---| | Nuclear radius | $R = R_0A^{1/3}$, $R_0 = 1.2$ fm | grows slowly with A | | Nuclear volume | $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi R³ ∪ A$ | proportional to A | | Nuclear density | $\rho = \dfrac{1.66×10^−27 A}{\frac{4}{3}\pi R_0³A}$ | ≈ 2.3×10¹⁷ kg/m³,…
